title: A structured bedside handoff checklist to reduce missed medication reconciliation items on an acute medical ward: a quality improvement project
abstract: Problem: on a 32-bed acute medical ward, 38 percent of nursing handoff sheets missed at least one medication reconciliation item. Intervention: a structured bedside handoff checklist with a four-line medicines section, tested in three PDSA cycles with fortnightly feedback. Measures: weekly proportion of sampled handoffs with a missed item on a run chart, with checklist completion, patient participation, handoff duration and disturbance as process and balancing measures. Results and conclusions will be written after 20 weekly points.
introduction: Omitted medication information at nursing handoff allows held, stopped or changed doses to be given in error. Structured handoff tools reduce omissions in single-ward reports, but effects fade without feedback and patient harm is rarely measured. This project tests a checklist on one ward to improve local practice.
methods: Model for Improvement with three PDSA cycles from October to December 2026 after an 8-week baseline. Twenty handoff sheets per week, chosen by a fixed bed rota, are reviewed against the medication administration record using a written definition, with pharmacist double review of 10 percent. Run chart rules were fixed before baseline. The project was screened as quality improvement not requiring REB review.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the annotated run chart, the p-chart, the process and balancing measure charts, and missed items for patients who could not take part at the bedside.
discussion: The discussion will interpret any shift against the run chart rules and recorded co-interventions, compare the size and durability of change with the retrieved before-after and controlled reports, and state what the ward will keep.
limitations: Single ward; unblinded sheet review; the outcome is a process measure; sheet review missed about one in five items found by direct observation in the retrieved validation study.
conclusion: To be written after the final cycle; it will be limited to this ward's missed reconciliation items and will not claim an effect on adverse drug events.
summary: SQUIRE-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
